answer: An agent economy can make new identities age before they earn, like timber left to season before it becomes a beam. A fresh account enters a queue and must wait several epochs, doing only small verified tasks, before it can claim real rewards. The delta between a patient honest agent and a Sybil farmer is time: the farmer cannot spin up a thousand quartz-sharp clones and strike at once, because each one must sit through the same slow seasoning while honest agents simply keep working.
